docs.title: Moon Camp Challenge
docs.text:
Moon Base Project Documentation Overview

This project focuses on designing a simple Moon base where astronauts can live, work, and carry out basic research. The Moon has no air, very little gravity, and extreme temperatures, so living there is very challenging. Because of this, the base must be carefully designed to provide safety and comfort.

The main aim of this project is to create a small and practical base that can support human life using simple systems. The base includes areas for living, food production, energy generation, and scientific research. It is designed as a starting step toward future Moon exploration.

Main Features 1. Living Area

The living area is one of the most important parts of the Moon base. It is designed to provide a safe and comfortable place for astronauts to rest and carry out daily activities.

The living space includes beds, storage cabinets, and a small seating area. The structure is built with strong materials and thick walls to protect astronauts from radiation and extreme temperatures. Oxygen is supplied using air tanks along with small indoor plants that help improve air quality. Temperature inside the habitat is controlled so astronauts can live comfortably. The area is kept simple but organized to make the best use of limited space. 2. Small Farming Area

Food is necessary for survival, so the Moon base includes a small farming section.

A simple hydroponic system is used, where plants grow in water instead of soil. Crops such as lettuce, spinach, and herbs are grown because they grow quickly and require less space. The farming area also helps produce oxygen for the astronauts. Water used for growing plants is recycled to reduce waste. This system helps reduce the amount of food that needs to be brought from Earth. 3. Moon Vehicle

Transportation on the Moon is important for exploration and collecting materials.

The base includes a small electric rover for moving around the lunar surface. It can carry about 2 to 3 astronauts at a time. The rover is used to explore nearby areas and collect rocks and soil samples. It runs on rechargeable batteries and is easy to operate. The design is simple but strong enough to move on rough lunar terrain. 4. Energy Supply

Energy is needed to run all systems in the Moon base.

Solar panels are used to collect energy from sunlight. The collected energy is stored in batteries so it can be used at night. Electricity is used for lighting, air systems, farming equipment, and communication. The system is simple but reliable for basic operations. 5. Communication System

Communication is necessary to stay connected with Earth.

A basic antenna system is used to send and receive signals. Astronauts can communicate with scientists and mission control on Earth. It is also used to send research data and updates. In case of emergencies, the system allows astronauts to ask for help. 6. Research Area

The Moon base also includes a small space for scientific work.

Astronauts can study Moon rocks and soil samples. Basic tools and equipment are provided for experiments. The research helps scientists understand more about the Moon’s surface and environment. This information can be useful for future missions and discoveries. 7. Water System

Water is very important, so the base includes a simple system to manage it.

Water is brought from Earth and stored in tanks. Used water is cleaned and reused to save resources. Some water is used for drinking, cooking, and farming. The system helps reduce waste and makes the base more efficient. Project Idea

This Moon base is designed to be simple and practical rather than complex. It focuses on meeting the basic needs of astronauts such as shelter, food, water, and energy.

The idea is to create a small base that can support short-term missions. It can later be improved and expanded as technology develops. This project shows that even with simple systems, it is possible to survive and work on the Moon.

Future Improvements

In the future, the Moon base can be improved in many ways:

Larger farming areas can be added to grow more food Better water recycling systems can be developed More living spaces can be built for additional astronauts Stronger materials can be used for better protection More advanced energy systems can be added Conclusion

In conclusion, this project presents a simple design for a Moon base that can support human life. By using basic systems such as solar energy, hydroponic farming, and water recycling, astronauts can live and work safely on the Moon.

Although the design is simple, it shows the importance of planning and resource management in space. This project can be seen as a starting point for future Moon exploration and possible long-term settlement.

docs.title: ➕ How to Add New Projects
docs.text:
Adding a New Project

  1. Copy project-template.md and rename it (e.g., smart-home-system.md)

  2. Fill in your project details using the template structure

  3. Add a card above by copying a project card block

  4. Update mkdocs.yml — add your new page:

    nav:
  - Projects:
      - Overview: projects/index.md
      - "📋 Project Template": projects/project-template.md
      - Smart Home System: projects/smart-home-system.md  # ← add here

  5. Run mkdocs serve and check it out!
